page: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-44-standardlssd is a storage-optimized compute instance designed for intensive database and storage-centric enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance incorporates an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz. It provides 44 dedicated vCPUs derived from 22 physical cores via symmetric multithreading, supported by 105 MB of shared Level 3 cache. The platform includes architectural features such as AVX-512 vector extensions, AMX matrix acceleration, and hardware-level AES cryptographic primitives. Memory capacity is configured at 352 GB, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU distribution that comfortably accommodates memory-heavy database working sets.

A core architectural feature is the inclusion of 9,663 GB of direct-attached NVMe local SSD storage distributed across three drives. In synthetic and real-world evaluation, the server exhibits strong throughput in multi-threaded decompression, achieving 230.59 GB/sec in bzip3 tests, as well as superior results in PassMark cryptographic evaluations. General-purpose processing metrics across Geekbench and PassMark reflect consistent mid-tier execution speeds. Prompt processing for smaller and medium language models demonstrates solid efficiency via CPU matrix capabilities, though text generation on 70B parameter models shows marked throughput limitations in the absence of discrete GPU hardware.

The dense resource configuration delivers solid qualitative cost efficiency for organizations requiring collocated compute, large RAM buffers, and high-capacity low-latency local storage on a single virtual host. Because the local NVMe storage is directly attached, workloads must implement application-level redundancy to manage ephemeral disk state. Overall, the server is particularly suited for high-throughput transactional databases, large-scale Redis or Memcached instances, distributed analytical clusters, and extract-transform-load (ETL) processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-44-standardlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine engineered for data-intensive processing and high I/O throughput. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz, it supplies 44 dedicated vCPUs across 22 physical cores alongside 105 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX instructions. Memory capacity is substantial at 352 GB, providing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-dense services. Storage performance is anchored by 9,663 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity across three local drives, eliminating reliance on external network volumes for high-rate operational datasets. Benchmark testing reveals strong multi-threaded decompression throughput and hardware-accelerated encryption, alongside balanced general compute performance across PassMark and Geekbench suites. Lacking dedicated GPU silicon, its large-model text generation is bounded, but CPU-based prompt processing remains efficient. This instance is strategically positioned for relational databases, NoSQL engines, distributed data stores, and real-time analytical workloads requiring substantial memory and dense local storage.
